q: Show me a chart of daily net sales against ad spend for October, and point out the days we spent a lot but sold little.
answer:
Chart created: daily net sales (by order date) vs ad spend (ad delivery date) for 2026-10-01 → 2026-10-29. The chart shows both series; ad spend is on the paid-media delivery clock while net sales are by order date.

Quick take: on several October days we spent more than our typical daily ad budget but got comparatively low sales (low ROAS). The days the data flags are: 2026-10-06, 2026-10-07, 2026-10-08 and 2026-10-09 — each had ad spend above the month’s average (₹48,453.6) while their ROAS was below the month’s median ROAS (1.3306).

What changed, briefly
- Mean daily ad spend (Oct 1–29): ₹48,453.6. Median daily ROAS (net sales ÷ ad spend): 1.3306.
- Flagged days:
  - 2026-10-06 — Ad spend ₹70,633.76 vs net sales ₹91,532.55 (ROAS 1.2959).
  - 2026-10-07 — Ad spend ₹71,171.66 vs net sales ₹81,201.99 (ROAS 1.1409).
  - 2026-10-08 — Ad spend ₹69,851.37 vs net sales ₹90,962.38 (ROAS 1.3022).
  - 2026-10-09 — Ad spend ₹60,101.69 vs net sales ₹53,879.73 (ROAS 0.8965).
- Why it matters: those days burned above-average ad budget but returned lower efficiency than a typical October day — 10–11 and especially 2026-10-09 show ROAS well under the median.

Worth checking:
- Campaign / ad-platform split for 2026-10-06 → 2026-10-09 to see which campaigns spent most and whether delivery or creatives changed.
- Any ad account edits (status/budget/bid) in that window and landing-page performance (sessions, LPVs, add-to-carts) for the same dates.

Period: 2026-10-01..2026-10-29 · Currency: INR · Data as of 2026-10-28
